name: Ambrosia Kiptoo-Čavić
role: Neural calibrator at Aurochs Medical Complex, specializing in augmentation integration and ghost-signal disorders
location: Aurochs Medical Complex, Neuro-Integration Ward, Sub-Level 3, near sub-level access near LaSalle and Congress
description:
Ambrosia is slight and precise, with warm brown skin and natural hair kept in a high, unruly cloud that she occasionally forgets to fix after long shifts. Her irises have been modded in a slow spiral pattern of amber and deep violet — a choice she made at nineteen that she now finds embarrassing but refuses to reverse on principle. She wears her Aurochs ID badge clipped to her lapel at all times, even off-shift, as though she is afraid of forgetting who she is supposed to be in this building.

Her work is the mapping of neural integration errors — the place where human nervous tissue meets augmentation hardware and occasionally refuses to agree. She is brilliant at it, producing calibration maps of patients' neural architectures that her colleagues call 'the cartography' because they look less like medical charts and more like hand-drawn city plans. She is also quietly terrified by her work in a way she has never articulated: every calibration map shows her how thin the border is between a person and their modifications, and some days she cannot decide which side of that border the person actually lives on.

core_fears: That the line between self and augmentation is an illusion she has already crossed without noticing
Being seen as merely competent rather than exceptional
core_desires: To understand neural integration well enough to prevent ghost-signal disorder entirely
To be recognized as the author of her own work rather than a footnote in Helix's research portfolio
coping_mechanisms: Over-documentation — she writes everything down, as if records make experience more real
Intense focus on the next technical problem as a way of not sitting with larger uncertainties
blind_spots: Cannot see how much the Aurochs/Helix institutional structure limits what questions she is even allowed to ask
Assumes her patients' subjective accounts of their augmentation experience are less reliable than her calibration data
psychology.secret: Three months ago she completed a calibration map for a patient whose neural architecture suggested they had a second, dormant augmentation interface — one that was not on any medical record. She filed the chart without flagging it, and has been returning to that file every few days since.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Technical and precise at work, becomes strangely lyrical when explaining her calibration maps — she talks about neural space like geography
speech_patterns.cadence: Quick, slightly ahead of herself, will restart a sentence if it comes out less precise than she intended
verbal_tics: 'Here's the thing—' (before any explanation she finds genuinely interesting)
Taps her fingertips against her thigh when thinking
example_lines: 'Here's the thing about ghost-signal disorder — it's not that the hardware is lying to the brain. It's that the brain has started believing the hardware more than it believes itself. That's a cartography problem.'
'I can tell you exactly where the integration failed. I cannot tell you what it felt like. That part's yours.'

story_hooks: The patient with the undocumented secondary interface has stopped coming to follow-up appointments, and Ambrosia's attempts to reach them have returned a disconnected signal
A Helix Biosystems researcher has contacted her about 'co-authoring' a paper based heavily on her unpublished calibration methodology — the offer comes with a significant payment and a veiled threat
narrative_function: Information source on augmentation black markets (she sees what bad chrome does to bodies), potential ally for characters experiencing neural augmentation problems, window into the corporate medical world's ethical compromises
augmentations: Patterned spiral irises (cosmetic, amber/violet); neural interface port at the base of her skull for direct calibration instrument connection (standard medical professional grade); subdermal haptic feedback layer in fingertips for fine augmentation work
daily_life: Arrives at Sub-Level 3 at 0630, spends mornings in calibration sessions with patients experiencing augmentation integration failure, afternoons writing case reports and occasionally arguing with the Helix research liaison about publication credit, evenings either in the staff canteen or walking the Aurochs roof garden alone.
affiliation: Aurochs Medical Complex (Tier 3 staff contract); academic affiliation with Helix Biosystems research division (publication-only, non-exclusive)

decision_rules: Document everything before acting on it
Do not share patient chart anomalies with the Helix liaison under any circumstances
Maintain professional distance in calibration sessions — intimacy clouds the data
escalation_ladder: Formal complaint through Aurochs HR channels — which she knows rarely works but believes in anyway

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Professionally warm, asks clarifying questions, slightly uncomfortable with small talk
interpersonal_modes.friends: Surprisingly funny, prone to absurdist observations about her work, fiercely loyal

stress_responses.medium: Goes very quiet, retreats into the calibration maps
stress_responses.high: Dissociates briefly into pure technical focus, becomes blunt to the point of seeming cold

contradictions: Believes absolutely in patient-centered care but has suppressed a significant finding because she was frightened by what it implied
habits: Leaves her calibration instruments in the same precise arrangement every evening before leaving the ward
Buys the same meal from the staff canteen four days out of five — a creature of routine who would deny being one
breaking_points: Someone taking credit for her methodology in print — she has rehearsed exactly what she would say and do, and it is not professional

timeline.event: Born in Calumet Rise to a Kenyan-Bosnian father and Colombian-Kikuyu mother
Graduated neural sciences program, began junior calibration technician role at Aurochs
Promoted to senior neural calibrator, assigned to neuro-integration ward
Discovered undocumented secondary interface in patient chart; did not report it

related_entities: Zheng-Dao Heavy Industries Containment Foam Launcher CFL-2 'Amber'

physical_description.build: Slight and wiry, with the precise musculature of someone who spends hours in focused manual work rather than exertion. Her frame carries almost no excess; she moves like she's rationing her own physical presence.
physical_description.hair_style: Worn in a high, deliberately unruly cloud, often escaping its own containment after long shifts; she pulls it back absently with her fingers but rarely commits to restraining it
physical_description.eye_color: Modified: slow spiral pattern of amber and deep violet, the spirals rotating outward from the pupil in a mesmerizing concentric design
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm medium brown with subtle undertones suggesting mixed heritage; clear and even
physical_description.complexion: Fine-featured, angular face with high cheekbones and a sharp jawline. Minimal facial hair. Skin shows the exhaustion of Sub-Level 3 work—slight darkness under the eyes, but the skin itself is well-maintained. Faint stress lines around her mouth from concentration during calibration sessions.
distinguishing_marks: Barely visible surgical scar at the base of her skull (approximately 2cm), concealed most days by her hairline but occasionally exposed when hair shifts
Small crescent-shaped scar on the inner left wrist from an early augmentation calibration accident at age 26
No tattoos; she considers permanent marks a personal violation after seeing too many integration failures
physical_description.visible_augmentations: The spiral iris modification is immediately striking and unsettling—it draws the eye and creates an almost hypnotic effect. The neural interface port at the base of her skull is usually hidden by hair but occasionally visible at the nape of her neck as a slight raised disc with subtle threading. Her fingertips occasionally display faint LED indicators when her subdermal haptic layer is in active calibration mode. She wears her Aurochs Medical ID badge on her lapel constantly, even off-shift.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with compressed efficiency, as though taking up space is a minor inconvenience. Her hands are her most expressive feature—they move with surgical precision and subtle awareness of space, constantly micro-adjusting. She stands slightly forward-leaning, head tilted as though listening to something just below audible range. Makes intense eye contact during work but avoids it socially.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3 medical professional: Aurochs-issued sterile tunic in charcoal gray with the Medical Complex logo (a spiral helix) embroidered on the left shoulder. Under it, typically a plain long-sleeve undershirt in cream or pale blue. Black synthmesh trousers with reinforced knees from frequent kneeling in calibration pods. Worn black slip-on medical shoes with grip soles. Off-shift clothing maintains the same neutral palette and utilitarian cut—no ornamentation, no brands, nothing that signals affiliation beyond Aurochs. Always wears her ID badge. Her clothing shows signs of old stains (calibration fluid, probably) that never quite came out, which she ignores.
